_notes.verification_status: bot_command, get_user_by_principal_name, and post_blocks_message confirmed in 5+ production recipes in a live Workato workspace, and re-confirmed by activation-testing a scratch recipe (wk recipes start). help_event confirmed by a human tester end-to-end: guessed name failed in the editor, tester located the real name via the editor's connector/trigger picker, corrected it, then fully activated the recipe, sent 'help' to the live bot in Teams, and confirmed the reply. new_message_event and new_event were both confirmed by the same tester directly selecting them from the connector's own trigger picker in the recipe editor (not activation-fired, but the picker only lists real triggers, and for new_event the editor additionally resolved and returned a full live extended_output_schema for the selected event type -- a materially stronger signal than a name merely accepting import). post_blocks_reply_message was confirmed the same picker-selection way. delete_message was confirmed by an actual job run reaching it and getting a real upstream Microsoft Teams API error (not a Workato-level unknown-action error) -- see the per-name notes below for details on each.
_notes.get_user_by_principal_name: Observed with two different input fields across different recipes: `principal_name` (email/UPN) in one recipe, `id` (Azure AD object ID, typically sourced from the bot_command trigger's context.from.aadObjectId) in three others. Both are real, live-verified inputs to the same action -- likely alternate lookup modes on one field, but no toggleCfg was captured in any of the source recipes to confirm that formally.
_notes.help_event: Trigger takes no input (confirmed: the editor shows 'no further setup needed'). context.from.aadObjectId -- the exact same path used on bot_command -- resolves and works identically here, confirmed by a full activation test: get_user_by_principal_name(id: context.from.aadObjectId) -> post_blocks_message(channel: that id) round-tripped a real reply in Teams. IMPORTANT naming-convention lesson: Workato's internal trigger name does NOT always match the doc's UI label in an obvious snake_case way -- 'New help message trigger' in the docs is `help_event` internally, not `new_help_message`. Do not assume any other still-unverified name below follows a predictable pattern from its doc label either.
_notes.new_message_event: Real internal name for the doc's 'New message trigger (beta)' -- another case of the doc label not matching the internal name (guessed `new_message`, actual is `new_message_event`). Confirmed via the editor's trigger picker (picker label: 'New message', description 'Triggers when a new text message is sent to Workbot'). Supports a trigger condition (`filter` block), matching the doc's optional channel-scoping feature. FULL real output schema confirmed live by a human tester dragging every datapill the editor's tree showed into a formula field, then reading the resulting real paths back out of the saved recipe JSON (all top-level unless noted): `messageId`, `messageText`, `timestamp`, `serviceUrl`, `conversationId`, `conversationType`, `sentFromId`, `sentFromName`, `userId`, `recipientId`, `recipientName`, and `attachments` (an ARRAY; each item has `contentType`, `contentUrl`, `name` directly, plus a nested `content` object with `downloadUrl`, `uniqueId`, `fileType`). The doc's earlier-guessed field names (`message_text`, `conversation_id`, snake_case) were WRONG -- the real names are camelCase (`messageText`, `conversationId`), yet another instance of doc labels not predicting the real shape. The `attachments` schema strongly resembles the doc's separate 'Files for Enterprise Workbot' file-object table, but appears here on new_message_event's own output -- whether it's actually populated on a non-Enterprise Workbot connection has not been tested (no message with a real attachment has been sent to trigger this live).
_notes.new_event: A single generic, polymorphic real-time-event trigger (picker label: 'New real-time event', description 'Triggers when selected event occurs in Microsoft Teams') -- NOT a family of separate triggers, one per event. Its `event_name` input is a live-search picklist (not a static enum); only 'Typeahead search' (`event_name` value `application/search`) returned a match in this workspace when searched, including with the terms tab/task/card/fetch/adaptive/compose. The Typeahead search event's schema was fully captured live (see SKILL.md / patterns/real-time-events.md): a top-level `from.aadObjectId` (note: top-level, NOT nested under `context` like bot_command/help_event), plus `conversation`, `channelData`, and a `value.queryText`/`queryOptions`/`dataset` object for the search request itself. Because no tab- or task-module-related event name surfaced in this connector instance, Tab opened trigger and Show tab using Adaptive Cards action (from Workato's own docs) appear to NOT be available on this bot at all, likely because those require an Enterprise Workbot tier/manifest (per the docs' own 'Enterprise Workbot' gating for tabs/files) that this connection isn't provisioned with -- this is a checked, live finding, not merely an unverified gap.
_notes.bot_command_parameters: Parameter `type`/`control_type` pairs confirmed in production: string/text, and date_time/date (with parse_output/render_input: date_conversion on the corresponding extended_output_schema entry). The `file` type mentioned in Workato's own Workbot-for-Teams documentation has not been observed in any recipe in this workspace and is NOT included here or assumed to work.
_notes.post_blocks_message_blocks: text_block's text_type has been observed as both body_text and custom (the latter paired with separator/style.isSubtle for a de-emphasized footer line). text_with_button_block's button_type has been observed as both submit (= doc's 'Run bot command', invokes a separate bot_command) and action_continue_flow (= doc's 'Continue recipe', suspends the SAME job until clicked or a timeout elapses, then continues in that same job with new datapills available). Neither of these is a new action/trigger name -- see SKILL.md's Block Types Reference for details.
_notes.post_blocks_message_action_continue_flow: Confirmed live via direct field selection + save in the editor. text_with_button_block fields for this button_type: `header_text` (optional), `text` (mandatory -- block's own text, distinct from the containing text_block's text, which persists as an inert leftover key if the block's Type was switched from plain text after already being filled in -- strip it, only the object matching block_type is rendered), `button_title` (mandatory), `button_id` (optional -- lets you distinguish which button was clicked when a message has more than one, matching up with the selected_block_id output below), `separator` (optional, string boolean). A sibling top-level input field `timeout` also appears on the action itself (NOT inside the block) once a continue_flow button exists -- an integer, in MINUTES (confirmed via the field's own UI hint: 'Default value is 43200 minutes', suffix 'minutes' -- do not assume seconds despite the JSON value being a bare number). On timeout expiry, the job continues automatically. New OUTPUT fields on this same post_blocks_message step once continue_flow is used (confirmed via live schema, not guessed): `conversation_id` (string, top-level) and `user_selection` (object: `selected_button`, `selected_block_id`, and a `user` object with `id`, `username`, `team_id`). The message's own `id` output (used by delete_message/message updates) does NOT appear in this expanded schema, but was confirmed to still resolve as a valid datapill by a human tester -- extended_output_schema in this connector is not exhaustive, same lesson as the `context` field elsewhere in this file. FULLY activation-tested end-to-end, click included: a human tester started a bot_command recipe using this exact shape, clicked the button in a live Teams message, and confirmed the follow-up delete_message step fired correctly using the message's `id` output and the trigger's `context.conversation.id`. See templates/self-deleting-message.json.
_notes.post_blocks_message: Output schema confirmed live via an actual job run: a single field, `{"id": "<message id string>"}`. Use this `id` output for `post_blocks_reply_message`'s or a later `post_blocks_message`'s `message_id_to_update` field (per Workato's docs' 'Message to update' feature) or as `delete_message`'s `message_id` input -- both field names for those downstream uses are still unconfirmed guesses, but this `id` value itself is now real.
_notes.post_blocks_reply_message: Real internal name for the doc's 'Post reply' action -- confirmed by direct selection in the connector's action picker (label: 'Post reply', auto-generated description: 'Post reply to user as Workbot', exactly matching the doc). Distinct from post_blocks_message (= 'Post message' -- see below): its input, captured with only the default `adaptive_card_width` field present (not yet fully configured/tested), notably has NO `channel`/recipient field, consistent with the doc's description of Post reply implicitly targeting wherever the invoking command was sent from. Per Workato's own docs, 'Post reply must always be paired with a Workbot command' -- expect this to require a bot_command or help_event trigger context, not a clock trigger. Its `blocks` field shape has not been confirmed yet, but is presumed identical to post_blocks_message's given the shared 'blocks' naming convention -- NOT yet verified.
_notes.delete_message: FULLY RESOLVED, activation-tested end-to-end in a live bot_command recipe. `message_id`: post_blocks_message's `id` output. `conversation_id`: `context.conversation.id` on the bot_command trigger itself -- found by a human tester expanding the trigger's live datapill tree (Context > Conversation > ID) after the earlier guess (a user ID from get_user_by_principal_name) was confirmed wrong via a live job failure ('Bad data sent to API server... Invalid message id or conversation id'). With the correct conversation_id, a human tester confirmed the full real-world behavior: the posted message visibly appeared in Teams and was then deleted. This is the same context path convention as bot_command's context.from.aadObjectId -- both live under context on this trigger's output, confirmed via the live datapill tree, not the (incomplete) extended_output_schema.
_notes.wait_for_interval_forbidden_in_workbot: IMPORTANT platform-level constraint discovered while building a real bot_command recipe: the base workato-recipes skill's clock/wait_for_interval action (see workato-recipes' patterns/wait-delay.md) CANNOT be used inside a recipe triggered by bot_command (and, given bot_command/help_event/new_message_event are all labeled 'Real-time' in the connector's own trigger picker, presumably help_event/new_message_event too, though only bot_command has been directly confirmed). Confirmed via an actual job failure with the exact platform error: 'Use of long actions is not allowed in WorkBot recipes'. This is a hard rule, not a guess -- do not suggest wait_for_interval (or presumably any other 'long action') inside a Workbot-triggered recipe. To pause before a follow-up action like delete_message, use a text_with_button_block with button_type action_continue_flow instead (see post_blocks_message_action_continue_flow above) -- it suspends the job until a button click or a configurable timeout, without violating this restriction, since waiting on user interaction is apparently not classified as a 'long action' the same way an unconditional timer is.
_notes.custom_action: Resolved, not a gap: the picker's 'Custom action' does NOT map to a connector-specific action named e.g. `custom_action` (the pattern some other custom connectors in this workspace use, e.g. Liferay's). Confirmed via direct selection + save in the editor: it is the standard `__adhoc_http_action` mechanism, identical to every other connector skill in this repo. No connector-specific documentation needed -- see the base workato-recipes skill's adhoc HTTP pattern docs.
_notes.post_simple_message: Real internal name for the doc's 'Post simple message' action. Confirmed by direct picker selection; captured with an empty input (no fields configured/tested yet). Per the doc, this is a reduced-feature sibling of post_blocks_message: Markdown-formatted plain text to a channel/user, no rich blocks/buttons.
_notes.post_simple_reply: Real internal name for the doc's 'Post simple reply' action. Confirmed by direct picker selection; captured with an empty input (no fields configured/tested yet). Per the doc, this is a reduced-feature sibling of post_blocks_reply_message: Markdown-formatted plain text reply, no rich blocks/buttons, no channel field expected (same 'replies where invoked' semantics as post_blocks_reply_message).
_notes.post_bot_message: Real internal name for the doc's 'Post message (old version)' action -- NOT `post_message`, another case of the doc label not predicting the internal name. Confirmed by direct picker selection; captured with a `use_json` field (string `"false"`) not present on post_blocks_message. This is very likely where the doc's 'Post as raw JSON' feature actually lives (fully custom Adaptive Card JSON via a `type: "message"` + `attachments` payload, per the doc) -- NOT on post_blocks_message, which has no such field. Presumed deprecated/legacy; lower priority than post_blocks_message for new recipes.
_notes.post_bot_reply: Real internal name for the doc's 'Post reply (old version)' action -- NOT `post_reply`. Confirmed by direct picker selection; captured with the same `use_json` field as post_bot_message, for the same likely reason (raw-JSON mode). Presumed deprecated/legacy; lower priority than post_blocks_reply_message for new recipes.
_notes.invoke_response: Real internal name for the doc-absent 'Response to real-time event' action (not mentioned anywhere in Workato's own Workbot-for-Teams documentation, same as new_event). Confirmed by direct picker selection, added as a step under a recipe whose trigger is new_event (Typeahead search event). FULL response-payload shape now confirmed live (both extended_input_schema and extended_output_schema materialized by the connector, not guessed): like new_event, this action is polymorphic -- `event_name` selects which event you're responding to (currently only `application/search` confirmed available, same constraint as new_event), and a same-named nested object (`"application/search": {...}`) holds the event-specific response. For application/search specifically: `type` (fixed/read-only, default `application/vnd.microsoft.search.searchResponse` -- the connector's own schema marks it `ngIf: false`, i.e. not user-editable) and `value.results`, an ARRAY of `{title, value}` objects (typically populated via a dynamic list datapill from a search/lookup action, per the doc's 'Using dynamic lists in action fields' pattern). This exactly matches Microsoft Bot Framework's public dynamic-search invoke-response format -- confirmed here against the live connector schema, not assumed from that external knowledge. NOT yet tested: an actual end-to-end round trip (a real Adaptive Card with a dynamic Input.ChoiceSet posted somewhere, a real user typing a query, and this action returning real results back into Teams) -- the schema is confirmed, the live behavior is not.
